sections.label: Industry workforce and demand
sections.summary: The industry struggles to meet growing demand for its services despite a 78,000-strong workforce across 1,700 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The industry is struggling to meet the growing demand for their services, even with a 78,000-strong workforce across 1,700 companies.

sections.label: Ages of cleaners and collectors
sections.summary: Local cleaners average 60 years old and local waste collectors 50, which is why the ES Industry Transformation Map was launched last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: On average, our local cleaners are 60 years old and our local waste collectors are 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: This is why we launched the ES Industry Transformation Map (ES ITM) last year.

sections.label: PWCS for large developments
sections.summary: New development applications for non-landed private residential developments with 500 Dwelling Units or more must implement PWCS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, we made it mandatory for new development applications for non-landed private residential developments with 500 Dwelling Units (DUs) or more to implement PWCS.

sections.label: First DPWCS at Kampong Bugis
sections.summary: The first District Pneumatic Waste Conveyance System under these amendments will be implemented at Kampong Bugis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We call this a District Pneumatic Waste Conveyance System (DPWCS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We will implement the first DPWCS under these amendments at Kampong Bugis.

sections.label: Space saved by no bin centre
sections.summary: NEA estimates a condominium with 1,000 Dwelling Units that no longer needs a bin centre saves space equal to one 5-room flat.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: NEA estimates that a condominium with 1,000 DUs that would no longer need a bin centre will save on space equivalent to one 5-room flat.

sections.label: Sections 31F and 31G scope
sections.summary: Section 31F limits new Part IIIA to premises not managed by Town Councils, and Section 31G lets the Minister declare DPWCS areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Section 31F will limit the new Part IIIA to premises which are not controlled or managed by a Town Council constituted under the Town Councils Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: There will thus be no change to the current arrangement where Town Councils manage PWCS in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Section 31G will allow the Minister to declare DPWCS areas where owners and occupiers of premises within the DPWCS area must use DPWCS.

sections.label: DPWCS licensing and works powers
sections.summary: Section 31J lets NEA license the DPWCS vendor, and section 31K sets out the licensee's powers to carry out necessary works.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Section 31J will provide powers to NEA to license the vendor that builds, operates or maintains the DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: For example, one of the licensing conditions that we will require the licensee to comply with is the Singapore Standard for PWCS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Section 31K sets out the powers of the DPWCS licensee to carry out necessary works for the purposes of the DPWCS.

sections.label: Mandatory connection to refuse pipeline
sections.summary: Under section 31L, the Director-General may require owners or occupiers in the declared area to connect to the refuse pipeline network.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Under section 31L, the Director-General will have powers to require owners or occupiers of premises within the declared area to connect to the refuse pipeline network.

sections.label: Connection charge and tariffs
sections.summary: The connection charge covers the DPWCS capital costs, while tariffs cover operating, maintenance and replacement costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The connection charge will cover the capital costs of the DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The tariffs will cover the operating, maintenance and replacement costs.

sections.label: Cleaner salary rise after PWM
sections.summary: Within two years of the PWM being mandated, the real median gross salary of a full-time resident cleaner rose from $1,100 to $1,200 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Within two years of the PWM being mandated, the real median gross salary of a full-time resident cleaner had risen from $1,100 per month to $1,200 per month.

sections.label: PWM Bonus for cleaners
sections.summary: With the PWM Bonus, some 40,000 resident cleaners may receive up to 4% more in wages each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the PWM Bonus, some 40,000 resident cleaners may receive up to 4% more in wages each year.

sections.label: Service of documents on officers
sections.summary: The amendments would allow these documents to be served on any other like officer of the company and at any location, besides its registered address.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The amendments would enable these documents to be served onto any other like officer of that company, and at any location, in addition to the registered address of that company.

sections.label: Higher fines for uncooperative offenders
sections.summary: Section 86 of the Act will be amended to raise the maximum fine for uncooperative offenders who withhold identification from $300 to $1,000 upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Amendments will also be made to section 86 of the Act to increase the penalties against uncooperative offenders who withhold their identification, from a maximum fine of $300 to $1,000 upon conviction.

sections.label: Repeal of sections 65 and 77
sections.summary: Sections 65 and 77 will be repealed so stiffer general penalties under section 103 apply, raising maximum fines for non-compliance in Parts VII and VIII from $2,000 to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To guard against these risks, sections 65 and 77 of the Act will be repealed so that stiffer penalties under section 103 of the Act, which provides for general penalties, will apply to offences under Parts VII and VIII respectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This will effectively raise the maximum fine for non-compliance for both Parts from $2,000 for a first conviction to $5,000, in line with other offences under the Act where penalties are not expressly provided for.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The remaining clauses 4 and 8 in the Bill are made for legal clarity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This Bill marks another milestone in our efforts to develop a productive ES sector that is innovative and forward-looking and provide good jobs with good pay for our workforce.

sections.label: Resident cleaners needing help
sections.summary: The passage identifies 46,000 resident cleaners as a vulnerable group needing help, working to keep the environment clean, safe and conducive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A vulnerable group that needs our help is the 46,000 resident cleaners who work tirelessly to ensure that we live in an environment which is clean, safe and conducive for all of us and our families to live, work and play.

sections.label: Past wage measures for cleaners
sections.summary: In 2014 the House passed the Environmental Public Health (Amendment) Bill introducing the mandatory PWM, and in 2016 TCC recommended wage increases averaging 4.6% per annum over six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2014, members of the House passed the Environmental Public Health (Amendment) Bill which boosted resident cleaners’ salaries through the introduction of the mandatory PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2016, the problem of wage stagnation and wage reset were partially addressed when TCC recommended a sustainable wage increase that would see the income of our general local cleaners grow at an average of 4.6% per annum over six years.

sections.label: Mandatory annual bonus for cleaners
sections.summary: One EPHA amendment mandates payment of an annual bonus to Singaporean and Permanent Resident cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One of the amendments of the EPHA is to mandate the payment of an annual bonus to Singaporean and Permanent Resident cleaners.

sections.label: Grace period for PWM Bonus
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that NEA give employers a one-year grace period, with a warning for non-compliance, for the PWM Bonus taking effect in January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Even though the cleaning industry has been given ample notice on the implementation of the PWM Bonus which will take effect in January 2020, I would like to propose to NEA to give the employers a grace period of one year where the employers would be given a warning should they fail to comply with the mandatory PWM Bonus.

sections.label: Tender clause for cleaners' wages
sections.summary: Service buyers can insert a tender clause so cleaners' wages and benefits are no worse off if the service provider changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, in line with this year’s National Wages Council recommendations, service buyers can do their part to help these cleaners by inserting a clause in their tender that the cleaners’ wages and benefits must be no worse off if they intend to change their service provider.

sections.label: Transforming industry and DPWCS framework
sections.summary: The speaker supports transforming the industry and a Bill proposal to introduce a framework to implement DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, we need to take concrete steps to transform the industry into a technologically-driven and skilled sector ready to meet the demands of the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am also supportive of another key proposal of the Bill, which is, to introduce a framework to implement DPWCS.

sections.label: Plans to mitigate DPWCS problems
sections.summary: The speaker asks what plans exist to mitigate problems faced by other countries that used the DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to ask what the plans are to mitigate the problems faced by other countries that had used the DPWCS.

sections.label: Mandatory PWM Bonus for resident cleaners
sections.summary: The speaker supports amendments making it mandatory for cleaning companies to give every resident cleaner a PWM Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This group is very hopeful that they can receive a bonus so that it can help defray the costs of living for their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the amendments to this Act because it will make it mandatory for cleaning companies to provide a PWM Bonus to every resident cleaner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Although the amount is equal to just two weeks' salary, this is an important first step because it ensures that this group of low-wage workers can receive a year-end bonus.

sections.label: Annual bonus for licensed cleaners
sections.summary: Licensed cleaning businesses must pay cleaners an annual bonus on top of wages, mandatory for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A licensed cleaning business will now be required to pay an annual bonus, on top of wages, to its cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will be mandatory for cleaners who are Singaporeans and Permanent Residents and is encouraged in the case of cleaners who are foreigners.

sections.label: Annual bonus with minimum amount
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Bill provisions instituting an annual bonus for cleaners with a minimum amount specified by the Commissioner of Labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this light, I welcome the provisions in this Bill instituting an annual bonus for cleaners, which will carry a minimum amount to be specified by the Commissioner of Labour.

sections.label: Extending PWM to more sectors
sections.summary: PWM was recently extended to lift technicians, and the speaker urges the Government to extend it to more sectors to support low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, PWM has very recently been extended to workers in a fourth sector: lift technicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Short of a national minimum wage plan pegged to household expenditures on basic needs, I urge the Government to take the lead in further adapting and extending its PWM to cover more sectors of our economy to better support more low-wage workers, so that they have, along with a ladder ahead of them, a floor beneath.

sections.label: PWCS funding and cleaner wages
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Government funding for PWCS installation, asks about grants for Town Councils' maintenance costs, and cites cleaner wage growth from 2012 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will benefit our cleaners, and we can benefit from a reduction in odour issues, improve overall hygiene and our living environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government is footing the bill for the installation of PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I ask if the Government will be providing any grants to the Town Councils to help offset the possible increased maintenance costs at least for the first few years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the Occupational Wage Survey conducted by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), it indicated that the median basic and gross wages of full-time resident cleaners grew by 9% and 12% per annum respectively from 2012 to 2015.

sections.label: PWM not mandatory for F&B cleaners
sections.summary: PWM is not mandatory for a cleaner hired directly by a food and beverage establishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, I understand that PWM is not mandatory for a cleaner who is hired directly by a food and beverage (F&B) establishment.

sections.label: Foreign cleaners and PWM application
sections.summary: The speaker asks what percentage of cleaners are foreigners and how many cleaning companies apply PWM to foreign cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what percentage of our cleaners are foreigners and how many cleaning companies actually apply the PWM to foreign cleaners?

sections.label: Higher-skilled worker licence condition
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether cleaning business licences could require 10% of foreign cleaners to be higher-skilled workers meeting experience, wage or certification requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Employers can upgrade their Basic-skilled R2 workers to Higher-skilled R1 workers by meeting minimum experience, minimum wage or certificate requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As incentives, employers pay a lower levy and enjoy an extended employment period for the Higher-skilled worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, at least 10% of construction workers must be higher-skilled R1 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Senior Minister of State consider similarly making it a condition of cleaning business licence that 10% of their foreign cleaners must be higher-skilled workers who again meet minimum working experience, minimum wage or certification requirements?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This could address my earlier point and might help us achieve higher productivity, improve profits and enjoy better service standards and quality in the cleaning sector.

sections.label: Mandatory PWCS use in designated areas
sections.summary: Proposed section 31G requires owners and occupiers of premises in designated DPWCS areas to use the area's PWCS, on pain of punishment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The proposed section 31G provides that when these areas are designated, owners and occupiers of every premises within the DPWCS area must use the PWCS for that area on pain of punishment.

sections.label: DPWCS exemption for Town Council
sections.summary: Section 31F of the Bill provides that the DPWCS will not apply to premises controlled or managed by the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet in this Bill, section 31F provides that the DPWCS will not apply to premises controlled or managed by the Town Council.

sections.label: Kampong Bugis DPWCS district
sections.summary: She earlier mentioned Kampong Bugis as the first district chosen for implementation of the DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier, she mentioned Kampong Bugis as the first district that has been chosen for the implementation of the DPWCS.

sections.label: Cost of mandatory DPWCS
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can indicate the expected cost of the mandatory DPWCS to existing homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government give any indication as to the expected cost of the mandatory DPCWS to existing homes?

sections.label: Residents' eventual bill compared
sections.summary: The passage asks what the eventual bill payable by residents will be compared to the current manual handling process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What will be the eventual bill payable by residents compared to the current manual handling process?

sections.label: PWCS cost and resident concern
sections.summary: A 2015 news report stated the PWCS costs over $11 million for Yuhua alone, and the speaker is concerned whether implementation costs will be passed to residents.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A news report in 2015 stated that the PWCS costs over $11 million, and this was for Yuhua alone.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More importantly, I am concerned about whether the cost for implementing the system will be passed on to residents in any form.

sections.label: Outreach, fines and PWM Bonus
sections.summary: The passage suggests deploying more officers to high-traffic areas on weekends for outreach and fines, and notes the Bill will mandate a PWM Bonus for resident cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Ministry can deploy more officers to high-traffic areas on weekends to conduct outreach and implement fines if offenders refuse to listen.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill will also mandate a PWM Bonus for resident cleaners.

sections.label: PWCS cost in Yuhua
sections.summary: PWCS can manage waste disposal better, sparing residents from stench and cockroaches, but costs $11 million to install in Yuhua alone.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   PWCS can manage waste disposal more effectively, sparing residents from the stench and cockroaches.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, it will cost $11 million to install this system in Yuhua alone.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If it is introduced island-wide, how much will it cost?

sections.label: Public cleanliness and littering
sections.summary: People should pick up litter themselves, as technology and cleaners cannot keep the environment clean if littering continues.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, after a meeting, we can pick up used cups or the litter on the table ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: No matter how good the technology is, and how many cleaners we have, if people continue to litter, our environment will still be dirty.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, we must treat the public space like our own home and maintain the virtue of environmental cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will help lighten the workload of our cleaners.

sections.label: Older employed residents and cleaners
sections.summary: Employed residents aged 62 and above rose 38% from 2013 to 2017, prompting questions on resident and foreign cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2017, the number of employed residents aged 62 and above rose by 38%, from 166,800 to 230,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the same period, those aged 67 and above jumped by 64%, from 61,700 to 100,900.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Of the employed residents aged 67 and over in 2017, 80% held secondary and lower qualifications, and 52% were employed as production and transport operators, cleaners and labourers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, specifically, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, in 2017, how many resident cleaners we have in Singapore; how many of the resident cleaners are aged 62 and above, and 67 and above; how many foreign cleaners we have; and what the average age of a foreign cleaner is.

sections.label: Feedback on suction noise and smell
sections.summary: Feedback was generally positive but raised concerns about suction noise and smell from choked pipes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The feedback is generally very positive but there were two concerns raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One is in relation to the sound of the system, the suction noise, and the other one is smell that may arise from time to time from choked pipes.

sections.label: DPWCS lifecycle cost question
sections.summary: A question was asked about the expected lifecycle cost of DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, on the issue of cost that was highlighted by the hon Member Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Ms Sylvia Lim, what would be the expected lifecycle cost of DPWCS?

sections.label: DPWCS connection and tariff charges
sections.summary: Sections 31M and N provide for connection and tariff charges under DPWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Will there be a similar situation under DPWCS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I further note that under sections 31M and N that there will be connection and tariff charges.

sections.label: DPWCS and compulsory annual bonuses
sections.summary: Implementing DPWCS and compulsory annual bonuses for Singaporean and PR cleaners is expected to bring a more productive and supportive work environment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the implementation of DPWCS and, more importantly, compulsory annual bonuses to our Singaporean and PR cleaners, we can look forward to a more productive and supportive work environment for our cleaners.

sections.label: PWCS as refuse collection game changer
sections.summary: The PWCS is described as a game changer for refuse collection, likened to the onsite sewerage system, with a London fatberg example.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The PWCS is thus a game changer for refuse collection, in much the same way the onsite sewerage system that we all took for granted was for waste collection just over 30 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, for instance, we read about how a monster "fatberg", which was 250 metres long and weighing 130 tonnes, blocked a sewer in London, and required about three weeks to dismantle, using pneumatic equipment.

sections.label: Residents' cooperation and PWM Bonuses
sections.summary: Residents' civic cooperation is needed to prevent blockages and keep the PWCS running, and mandatory PWM Bonuses for all cleaners are supported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And here we need all residents’ civic cooperation to prevent blockages and keep the PWCS functioning smoothly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am also happy to support the payment of mandatory PWM Bonuses to all our cleaners, whether they are hired directly by organisations or work at contracting companies.

sections.label: Mandatory PWM Bonus for cleaners
sections.summary: The proposed PWM Bonus mandates cleaning companies pay an annual bonus to Singaporean and PR cleaners, sharing economic gains more equitably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed PWM Bonus will mandate that cleaning companies must pay out an annual bonus to our Singaporean and PR cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is good news for our cleaners whose work is often undervalued, and wages tend to be sticky because of competitive market forces and workers' lack of bargaining power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This bonus ensures that economic gains are shared more equitably with them.

sections.label: Cleaners' awareness and CPF flagging
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry will ensure cleaners know of the mandatory bonus and suggests working with CPF to flag non-paying companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How can the Ministry ensure that the cleaners are aware of this mandatory bonus?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And since this bonus is mandatory, I suggest that the Ministry work with CPF to flag out companies that do not pay the PWM Bonus.

sections.label: Enforcement against motorist litterbugs
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry works with MOT for LTA and MHA for Traffic Police on strict enforcement against errant motorist litterbugs causing roadside fires.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I hope the Ministry can work with the Ministry of Transport for LTA, and the Ministry of Home Affairs  for the Traffic Police, to implement strict enforcement actions that can effectively deter such errant motorist litterbugs from littering our roads and causing inconvenience by starting bush or shrub fires on central road dividers or road sides, when they throw their cigarette butts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Such roadside and road divider fires number about 350 a year.

sections.label: High-rise litterbug CCTV cameras
sections.summary: NEA lacks enough cameras to catch high-rise litterbugs, with deployment limited to five to seven days per location, and the MP asks if more will be deployed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As for high-rise litterbugs, while NEA is trying its best to be able to catch these litterbugs in the act through the deployment of video cameras or closed-circuit television (CCTV), I understand that there are insufficient video cameras or CCTVs available to be deployed for such purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is to the extent that the duration in which a particular video camera or CCTV can be deployed is limited to just five to seven days at any one particular location.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry be investing in and deploying more of such video cameras or CCTVs for the purpose of catching highrise litterbugs in the act?

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for cleaners
sections.summary: The speaker addresses the introduction of the Progressive Wage Model for cleaners, highlighted in clauses 2, 6 and 7 of the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The second area I would like to speak on is the introduction of the PWM for Cleaners, as highlighted in clauses 2, 6 and 7 of the amendment Bill.

sections.label: Connection charge covers capital costs
sections.summary: The connection charge will cover the capital costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, the connection charge will cover the capital costs.

sections.label: Monthly tariff from premises owners
sections.summary: A monthly tariff will be collected from owners of premises within the district, such as the MCSTs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Second, a monthly tariff will be collected from owners of premises within the district, such as the MCSTs.

sections.label: Singapore waste generation growth
sections.summary: Waste generation in Singapore grew from 5.6 million tonnes in 2007 to 7.7 million tonnes in 2017, a 40% increase over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Waste generation in Singapore grew from 5.6 million tonnes in 2007 to 7.7 million tonnes in 2017, a 40% increase over the last decade.

sections.label: DPWCS cost at Kampong Bugis
sections.summary: The cost per dwelling unit for the DPWCS at Kampong Bugis is expected to be lower than at Yuhua, a brownfield site requiring costly retrofitting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For these reasons, we expect the cost borne by each dwelling unit (DU) for the DPWCS at Kampong Bugis to be lower than that at Yuhua, which is a brownfield site that required extensive and more costly retrofitting works, as mentioned by Er Dr Lee Bee Wah.

sections.label: Singapore Standard for PWCS
sections.summary: NEA is jointly developing a Singapore Standard for PWCS with HDB, ESG and other stakeholders, covering proper maintenance such as replacing air filters every six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To address this, NEA is jointly developing a Singapore Standard for PWCS with HDB, Enterprise Singapore (ESG) and other stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Standard covers proper maintenance of PWCS, such as recommendations to replace air filters every six months, so that they remain effective in removing unpleasant odours.

sections.label: Fault detection and contingency plans
sections.summary: Members highlighted prompt fault detection and contingency plans for PWCS breakdowns, and NEA will ensure reliable waste collection through licensing conditions on the DPWCS licensee.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Mr Zainal Sapari, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Irene Quay highlighted the need for prompt detection of faults in the PWCS and the importance of contingency plans in the event of breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It is our priority that our residents have reliable waste collection services and NEA will ensure this through licensing conditions on the DPWCS licensee.

sections.label: Temporary grant to Town Councils
sections.summary: MND is providing a temporary grant to Town Councils to help offset costs until the PWCS industry attains economies of scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For example, as mentioned by Mr Murali Pillai, MND is providing a temporary grant to Town Councils to help offset costs until the PWCS industry attains economies of scale.

sections.label: Enhancing PWCS development and management
sections.summary: With experience gained, PWCS development and management in Singapore will continue to be enhanced with relevant agencies on suitable areas, considering site, technical and financial factors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the experience gained, we will continue to enhance the development and management of PWCS in Singapore by working with the relevant agencies on suitable areas, taking into account site, technical and financial considerations.

sections.label: DPWCS in landed estates
sections.summary: There are currently insufficient economies of scale to implement DPWCS in landed estates for the system to be financially viable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Currently, we do not think that there are sufficient economies of scale to implement DPWCS in landed estates for the system to be financially viable.

sections.label: Cleaning workforce profile
sections.summary: There are more than 40,000 resident cleaners and 17,000 foreign cleaners, with average ages of 60 and 37 years old respectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Louis Ng asked about the profile of the cleaning workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: There are currently more than 40,000 resident cleaners and 17,000 foreign cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Their average age is 60 years old and 37 years old respectively.

sections.label: Cleaning tools and supervisor training
sections.summary: NEA and Workforce Singapore jointly developed enhanced tools, chemicals and machines, and cleaning supervisors can receive training under the Environmental Cleaning WSQ framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA and Workforce Singapore have jointly developed a list of enhanced tools, chemicals and machines that businesses can adopt to make cleaning more effective and safe for cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Cleaning supervisors can also receive training under the Environmental Cleaning Workplace Skills Qualification (WSQ) framework to implement risk controls and educate workers on workplace safety.

sections.label: Mandating minimum R1 cleaner proportion
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng proposed mandating a minimum proportion of R1 foreign cleaners, and this suggestion will be studied with MOM.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng also proposed mandating a minimum proportion of R1 foreign cleaners; we will study this suggestion with MOM.

sections.label: Penal Code litter embers clause
sections.summary: The Penal Code Review Committee proposed a new clause linking those who litter materials containing embers to a fire that subsequently occurs at that place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Penal Code Review Committee has proposed to introduce a new clause linking those who litter materials containing embers to a fire that subsequently occurs at that place.
